title: engage-week-scenario-catalog-and-exec-lines-v0-1
body:
Purpose:
This is a working catalog for 'Engage Week' — a compact company-wide sequence (one week) combining an exec update, OKR alignment, and an interactive all-hands. Goal is to align leadership narrative, surface cross-team blockers, and leave each functional team with 2–3 clear commitments for the coming quarter.

Context / constraints:
- Timing: target week = 2025-08-04 to 2025-08-08 (internal planning window).
- Audience: all employees; primary listeners are eng, product, sales, CS, and SRE leads.
- Tone: candid, production-first (we call out tradeoffs), with clear asks.
- Risk: avoid heavy feature-level slides; focus on measurable team-level asks.

High-level run-of-show (draft):
- Day 0 (pre-week): leader huddles (execs + POs) to finalize talking points and rollout plan. Owners: Asha (prod-ops), Leah (comms).
- Day 1: Exec update (45m) — CEO + CTO + Head of Product: company health, capacity, top 3 risks, customer signals, clear ask. 20m for live Q&A.
- Day 2: OKR clinic (60m) — short walkthrough of proposed company OKRs + breakout rooms per function to align KRs. Owners: Marcus (growth), Diego (eng).
- Day 3: Solutions spotlight (30m) — 3 short product demos from teams with biggest customer/regulatory impact. Owner: Eng leads.
- Day 4: Triage & Commitment session (60m) — triage outstanding blockers (infra, capacity, compliance). Each team commits to 2 actions. Owners: SRE/Product-Ops.
- Day 5: Public wrap + comms launch (30m) — close, publish OKRs and team commitments, update Confluence. Owner: Comms.

Draft company OKRs (working — feedback welcome):
- Objective A: Make inference predictable and cost-efficient for SaaS customers
  - KR1: Reduce median 95th-percentile latency for hosted text-generation by 15% across top-10 models (measured by production telemetry).
  - KR2: Decrease per-token inference cost for typical PLG query mix by 12% using batching/caching/quantization levers.
  - KR3: Reach 3 enterprise trials on Dedicated with SLA attachments (>$50k ARR pipeline).

- Objective B: Ship Private deployment primitives that enable regulated customers to onboard faster
  - KR1: Reduce average provisioning time for VPC private stacks from 12 days -> 4 days (automation + runbook improvements).
  - KR2: Achieve SOC2 readiness checklist completion for Private deployments (core 80% items) and start two customer audits.
  - KR3: Document 5 reference network/topology patterns and publish how-to templates.

- Objective C: Developer experience & observability to reduce incidents and accelerate rollouts
  - KR1: Ship token-level cost/latency dashboard beta to 50 customers and 100 internal teams.
  - KR2: Cut mean time to detect regression (model quality or perf) from 10 days -> 3 days via evals + alerts.
  - KR3: Reduce rollouts that require manual rollback by 40% through automated fallback policies.

Notes on KRs (quick rationale):
- A focus on 95th-percentile latency aligns with our SLOs and customer pain.
- Cost reductions emphasize practical levers (batching, cache TTL, quantization) and should tie to concrete playbooks.
- Private onboarding KRs are intentionally operational (time-to-provision) because sales adoption is sensitive to turnaround.

Communication plan (external/internal cadence):
- Pre-week (internal): short memo (Asha) + one-pager of talking points for execs. Slack channel: #engage-week-2025 (Leah to create).
- During week: live stream + recording posted to Confluence/Drive; short daily recap email for execs and managers.
- Post-week: publish OKR canonical page, update roadmap artifacts, and send follow-up to customers with relevant signals (CS).

Exec talking points (shortform):
- CEO: state of the business: ARR trends, top 5 customer signals, what we will protect vs. where we will iterate. Ask: support prioritization decisions during triage.
- CTO: technical posture: latency/cost trajectory, capacity headroom, and mitigation plan for top infra risk. Ask: engineering reps to back quick wins and test automation tickets.
- Head of Product: product priorities and KR map. Ask: PMs to finalize minimal scope for each team commitment.

Breakout room prompts for OKR clinic:
- Is the KR measurable and tracked (owner + metric)? If not, propose immediate telemetry needed.
- What are the top 2 risks to achieving this KR this quarter? (capacity, dependency, customer readiness).
- What is the single most important experiment or playbook that would move the needle?

Triage rubric (for Day 4):
- Impact (customer-facing severity or ARR risk): High/Med/Low
- Effort (dev + infra days): Quick (<3d), Medium (3–10d), Long (>10d)
- Dependencies: cross-team blockers flagged with owner and required decision
- Decision rule examples: If Impact=High and Effort=Quick => prioritize now. If Impact=Med and Effort=Long => consider scheduled backlog.

Runbook & materials (owner pointers):
- Exec slide deck (work-in-progress): github:repo/inference-playbooks/presentations/engage-week-deck (Diego).
- OKR canonical page (to publish day 5): confluence:ENG-OKR-2025-Q3 (Asha).
- Recordings and transcripts: Drive folder (Leah to create).

Risk register (initial):
- R1: Capacity crunch if Dedicated demand spikes mid-week -> mitigation: throttle new Dedicated trials for 72h and enable fallback to hosted variants (SRE + Sales coordination). Owner: SRE lead.
- R2: Messaging mismatch between exec and product -> mitigation: two pre-recorded rehearsals and a 1:1 run with CEO+CTO (Asha to schedule).
- R3: Too many tactical asks drown strategic priorities -> mitigation: cap team commitments to 2 items; require alignment to KRs.

Open questions we need to answer before publishing OKR draft:
- Q1: Measurement definitions: who is responsible for the instrumentation tasks to track latency and cost KRs? (Suggest: Observability -> Marcus; Eng infra -> Diego).
- Q2: External comms: do we include specific customer examples in the all-hands or keep public messaging abstract? (Recommend: abstract, with CS doing targeted outreach).
- Q3: What is success for the week? Proposed: all teams publish commitments and 70% of teams have clear owners on KRs.

Immediate next steps (this doc is a working checklist):
- [ ] Leah: create #engage-week-2025 Slack and draft pre-week memo (due 2025-07-15).
- [ ] Diego: finalize deck skeleton and send to exec reviewers (due 2025-07-18).
- [ ] Marcus: validate telemetry availability for latency/cost KRs and list missing events (due 2025-07-17).
- [ ] Team leads: nominate 2 reps per functional breakout (due 2025-07-20).

Comments / notes to self (informal):
- Keep the deck visual, one metric per slide; avoid long bulleted product specs.
- Prep a short script for CEO 2–3 lines that call out tradeoffs (e.g., performance vs. cost vs. time-to-market).
- Consider a short customer panel during Day 3 if CS can surface 2 users who would speak to reliability gains.

Document history / edits: 
- v0-1 (2025-07-08) initial skeleton (Asha).
- v0-2 (2025-07-14) added OKR draft and run-of-show (collaborators: Diego, Leah).
- v0-3 (2025-07-22) added triage rubric and immediate to-dos (Asha).

If you're reviewing: please add inline notes in Drive and ping me in DMs for decisions that need exec input.

-- Asha
